claims.public_wording: Yuho parses the checked-in Singapore Penal Code corpus and the covered DSL fragment.
limits: Parsing success does not establish legal or semantic fidelity.
Known grammar regressions are release-blocking defects.

claims.public_wording: Yuho checks runtime/Z3 agreement on retained fixtures for the documented subset.
limits: This is not a proof of every Yuho program, every backend, or legal correctness.

claims.public_wording: Yuho has mechanised checks for documented Lean fixtures and structural obligations.
limits: There is no end-to-end refinement proof from the production runtime to a formal semantics for the full DSL or corpus.

claims.public_wording: Each checked-in Penal Code encoding is linked to a repository raw-source snapshot and machine-verifiable raw-section and .yh file hashes.
limits: A checked-in snapshot is not independent confirmation of the current official statute text or legal interpretation.
The legacy ledger does not yet contain the immutable raw-byte snapshots, source spans, canonical-IR hashes, or independent approvals required by the target corpus-evidence schema.

corpus_review.certification_rule: Only a record explicitly labelled human review counts as human-reviewed. Automated and unattributed records are not legal certification.

prohibited_public_claims: A broad formal-methods claim without naming its covered semantics and proof boundary.
A claim that every Penal Code section has human review.
A claim that successful analysis proves legal correctness or provides legal advice.
A semantic-equivalence claim for an export backend without matching evidence.
